title: Open a shelf-ready tray of cans: peel its perforated front panel out and down from a top corner so it tears cleanly
instruction: Tear the perforated front panel completely off the tray of cans, lay the torn panel flat on the bench clear of the tray, and leave all six cans standing upright inside the tray on its marks.
context: Stockers and order fillers (O*NET 53-7065.00, about 2.8 million US workers, BLS OEWS) restock supermarket aisles all shift using shelf-ready corrugated trays whose perforated front display window is torn off by hand without a blade so the tray goes straight onto the shelf with cans faced. By our estimate only one pull tears it: lifting straight up loads the whole bottom perforation in plane (estimated about 460 N from published perforation indices and the board's grammage), so it holds and an unbraced tray tips; a flat outward pull is estimated to tear only the two side seams (about 5.5 N), folding the panel down without freeing it. The stocker pinches one upper corner of the folded front header, turns it and peels outward and downward so the perforation unzips from corner to corner (estimated about 2.75 N over an 85 mm arc), while the six cans keep the tray on its marks.
setup: Station bench; cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x away from the arms, y left. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. Single fixed layout; nothing varies by seed. Six unopened Mutti Polpa Finely Chopped Tomatoes 400 g steel cans (73.0 mm diameter, 110.0 mm height, 454 g each) stand upright in a 3 x 2 grid inside a shelf-ready tray made from 3 mm single-wall B-flute kraft board (405 g/m2; or any 3 mm single-wall B-flute board of about 400 g/m2) to the bundled 1:1 dieline tray_template.svg (recipe in the reset notes): 230 x 164 x 130 mm outside, 28 mm fixed front lower lip, 218 x 102 mm tear-off front panel on a 6 mm cut / 2 mm tie perforation, its top 18 mm folded double to 6.0 mm; 55 g tray and 11 g panel. Tray centered at (28.0, 0.0) +/- 0.5 cm, front panel facing the arms (-x) at x = 19.8 cm, registered inside four 30 x 30 mm matte yellow gaffer-tape corner L-marks. A 16.0 x 26.0 cm grey outline on the right bench centered at (30.0, -28.5) +/- 0.5 cm marks a clear placement area. Checked against the corner marks and top-camera start photo.
scoring: Read when the trial ends; once the 1.0 state has held 1.0 s (20 steps), a further 3.5 s hold ends the trial early with both arms parked. Whole-trial zero rules (checked from the trial video; final photo confirms end state): 0.0 permanently if the tray base ever tilts > 10.0 deg from horizontal, its floor center lifts > 15.0 mm above the bench, or any of its 4 outer corners shifts > 25.0 mm horizontally from its start tape mark; or if any of the 6 cans ever tips > 12.0 deg from vertical or leaves the tray. Otherwise: 1.0 if the perforated front panel is completely detached, lying flat on the bench (<= 15.0 deg from horizontal, center <= 20.0 mm above bench top, set square/ruler), horizontally clear of the tray footprint by >= 30.0 mm (nearest edge gap, ruler) and not touching the tray, all 6 cans stand upright (<= 10.0 deg) inside the tray, tray corners are within 25.0 mm of start marks, both grippers are >= 30.0 mm clear of tray, cans and panel, and all bodies stay at rest (< 10.0 mm/s, < 0.10 rad/s) for 1.0 s (20 steps). 0.5 if at least half of the 422 mm perforation is torn (for example both side seams), by ruler, or the panel is detached without meeting every 1.0 placement, clearance or rest rule, while all 6 cans stand upright (<= 10.0 deg) in the tray within 25.0 mm of marks. 0.0 otherwise (less than half torn, including idle). The simulator tracks the tear in 10 equal stages (half = 5 of 10).
reset_notes: Tray recipe, one fresh tray per trial (never taped or reused): print tray_template.svg at 1:1 (550 x 495 mm: on a plotter, or tiled on A4 at 100 % scale and taped together) and lay it on the board; cut the solid outline with a utility knife along a steel rule; crease the blue dashed fold lines with a blunt edge (the back of a table knife or an empty ballpoint) against the rule; perforate the red dash lines by knife into 6 mm cuts with 2 mm ties, about 53 over the 422 mm (27 along the bottom, 13 up each side), or cut and perforate the whole sheet on a cutting plotter from the SVG; fold the walls up and glue the four glue flaps with a hot-melt glue gun, holding each flap until the glue has cooled and set (about a minute). About 20 minutes per tray by hand, about 5 with a cutting plotter (our estimates). Reset: lift the 6 unopened steel cans out of the opened tray, place them upright in a fresh tray, set the filled tray inside the 4 yellow corner L-marks and remove the old torn panel: under 1 minute with trays made ahead. Unopened steel cans are dry and clean; inspect for dents before reuse.
fidelity: Rigid bodies at true size: cans per the maker (400 g net) and listings (454 g gross, 73/110 mm tin); tray from the dieline in 3 mm B-flute board (maker's data sheet, 405 g/m2). A bilateral 3-joint chain + weld models the perforation; its forces are estimates from indices of perforated three-layer E-flute board (320-409 g/m2), applied to our B-flute by grammage: 459 N straight lift (never reached), 5.5 N flat pull (side seams only), 2.75 N corner peel. Not modelled: fibre jaggedness, flute crush.
